qt: to the Commission Konstantinos Arvanitis (The Left) Subject:

According to reports, the ‘Archipelagos’ Institute has filed a petition with the European Public Prosecutor's Office regarding ongoing cases of fraud and misuse of EU funds within the framework of the Greek Operational Programme for Fisheries and the Sea (OPFS) 20142020 which were channelled into Greece in the period 2021-2026. According to the available information, at least EUR 52 million intended for fisheries support were allegedly channelled – in violation of their functional purpose – to businesses unrelated to fisheries, in breach of the stipulated eligibility criteria. The above comes at a time when a series of similar scandals are weighing on the public sphere in Greece. In view of this: 1.
Has the Commission become aware of the case in question in any way?

Regardless of any independent criminal investigation into the matter, has the Commission ever taken action within the framework of its audit and supervisory responsibilities regarding the management and absorption of the specific funds? If not, will the Commission do so immediately following the revelations in question?
How does the Commission intend to improve the protocol for early detection and intervention in payment systems and in checks on relevance and fulfilment of obligations?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.11.2026) Investigations concerning fraud, corruption or other illegal activities affecting EU funds fall under the jurisdiction of the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF) and/or the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO). EPPO is responsible for investigating and prosecuting crimes affecting the financial interests of the Union and, as an independent body, it does not inform the Commission about the exercise of its competence. It is only in specific circumstances1 that the EPPO would share certain information with the Commission. It is however, not for the Commission to comment on possible complaints submitted to the EPPO. Under the framework of the European Maritime and Fisheries Fund2 (EMFF) 2014–2020, support delivered through Community-Led Local Development (CLLD) was designed for a broader local partnership and territory through fisheries Local Action Groups, which brought together public authorities, private actors and civil society to implement locally tailored development strategies. The target group is therefore wider than professional fishers, and can include among others local businesses, community organisations and public bodies, where their projects contribute to the objectives of the local CLLD strategy, in line with the objectives in the EMFF Regulation. For programmes implemented under shared management, the Commission does not select nor approve individual projects; it approves national programmes prepared by the Member States, carries out system audits on their management and control systems and oversees their overall implementation in line with the set objectives and the applicable EU provisions. Member States are to implement the programme in accordance with the principle of sound financial management3.
1 Provided for in Articles 26(2) and 103 of Regulation (EU) 2017/1939. 2 Regulation (EU) No 508/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 15 May 2014 on the European
Maritime and Fisheries Fund, OJ L 149, 20.5.2014, Articles 60-63. 3 Article 125(1) of the Common Provisions Regulation https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2013/1303/oj/eng.
